model: Bank residual income on tangible book, run as FCFE at cost of equity (engine route): NI to parent less CET1 retention, net debt zero, BRL flows, per ADS

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (FY2020 142,993 -> FY2025 204,501, owners of the parent); agrees with base revenue/RWA growth of ~7% and with 1 - payout(72%) x ROTE(~25%) = ~7%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (6.8-7.4%) diverges by more than 30% from NI/EPS CAGRs (15-19%). Cause: ROE rose from 13.5% (FY2020 COVID trough) to ~22-25% while a 70%+ payout plus the FY2025 R$48.3bn distribution kept book growth near 7%. The 5yr NI/EPS CAGRs start from the trough and are not forward rates. EPS CAGRs are restated to today's share basis (FY2022 R$2.66, FY2020 R$1.70 vs FY2025 R$4.05).
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs null: the CSV carries no revenue for this bank by design; managerial operating revenues were flat in FY2025 (175.1 vs 174.7) and +5.9% in 1H26. Owner-FCF CAGRs are not computed: bank OCF/FCF reflects deposit and loan flows, not owner earnings.

scenario_narratives.base: Itaú stays Brazil's best-run large bank but does not get better: 2026 guidance is met (loans ~+8-10%, client NII accelerating in H2, fees +2-5%), revenue grows 7-8% for five years as Selic cuts revive credit, and digital competitors slowly erode fee and card economics so NI/revenue drifts from 26% to 24.5%. ROTE ~25% now, ~23.7% at year 10; CET1 held at 12.3% and ~70-74% of earnings distributed. Exit ~2.0x tangible book, the stock's historical median.
scenario_narratives.bull: A credible post-election fiscal anchor lets Selic fall to ~10%: funding costs fall faster than asset yields, cost of credit eases, efficiency improves toward 35%, and loan growth runs ~10% for three years. ROTE rises to ~27-28% and the market pays ~2.5x tangible book, the 2018-19 peak.
scenario_narratives.bear: Fiscal slippage after the October 2026 election forces Selic back up, BRL sells off, and an over-indebted consumer pushes cost of credit toward 4%: NI falls ~20% in year 2 and ROTE troughs ~19%. Recovery is partial because Nubank/Inter/C6 permanently take fee and card share; ROTE settles ~20.5% and the stock re-rates to its 2021/2024 trough of ~1.5x tangible book.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Itaú is valued as a bank: residual income on tangible book, expressed as the cash its owners can take out (NI to owners of the parent less the CET1 retained to hold 12.3% of RWA as the balance sheet grows) discounted at a 15% BRL cost of equity, with deposits as operating funding (net debt = 0). Value = R$17.18/share tangible book + the PV of ROTE above the 15% CoE. Everything is in BRL until the final per-ADS conversion at spot (1 ADS = 1 preferred share). The judgment that matters is how long ~24% ROTE persists against Nubank and a Selic cycle, and the BRL cost of equity: the price implies ~13.7%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: each 1pp off the 15% BRL CoE adds roughly 12-15% to value; the market price implies ~13.7%.
Brazil fiscal/election risk (Oct-2026): drives Selic, BRL and credit costs together; the bear path.
BRL/USD: values are converted at spot 5.2223; a 10% BRL move changes the USD value per ADS 10% independent of operations.
Digital competition (Nubank > Itaú in customer count; fee guidance cut 5-9% -> 2-5%): the base fades NI/revenue 1.5pp over ten years.
Capital: CET1 fell 13.1% -> 12.3% YoY; a BCB tightening or Basel III phase-in would raise retention and cut distributable cash.
Data: IFRS ETR (~10% in 1H26) is distorted by the overseas-investment hedge; the 28% tax rate is a calibration to after-tax NI, not a forecast of cash tax.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for ITUB at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 6.54-9.60. Local cross-check ITUB4.SA (52-week 35.88-49.67) and BRL=X from the same API; see inputs.adr_parity_check and inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: Itaú Unibanco 20-F FY2016-FY2025 and IFRS condensed interim statements Q3-2025, Q4-2025, Q1-2026, Q2-2026 (research/ITUB/Extracted): Q2-2026 balance sheet (equity to parent 217,779; goodwill & intangibles 26,313; NCI 10,247), income statement (1H26 NI to parent 23,615; diluted shares), capital note (CET1 194,742, RWA 1,581,951, 12.3%), managerial highlights (operating revenues 1H26 93.4bn, FY25 175.1bn). History from ITUB_Metrics.csv. Historical P/B from Yahoo ITUB4.SA quarterly closes (split-adjusted) against IFRS BVPS restated to today's share basis.
data_sources.qualitative: ITUB_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): Q2-2026 results, 2026 guidance (fees cut to 2-5%), Selic path, Colombia/Panama exit, buyback.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted shares = ADS-equivalents (1 NYSE ADS = 1 preferred share). Q2-2026 weighted diluted shares 11,145.9M (5,617.7M common + 5,528.2M preferred, Q2-2026 IFRS interim income statement); 11,026.9M shares issued at 2026-06-30 (Note 19a), ~11,021M in circulation after treasury. Bonus issues (Nov-2018 3:2, Mar-2025 10%, Dec-2025 3%) are already reflected; the count is held FLAT because SBC (~0.1% of revenue) is expensed inside the flow and buybacks (200M-pref programme to Aug-2027) are the distribution of the flow, value-neutral.
inputs.adr_parity_check: 2026-10-02 closes: ITUB4.SA R$44.83 / BRL=X 5.2223 = US$8.584 vs ITUB ADR US$8.59 -> parity within 0.1%, confirming 1 ADS = 1 preferred share. ITUB3 (common) closed R$48.92, a ~9% premium to the preferred; the model values every share at the same economic claim (preferred have dividend >= common and 80% tag-along).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F cash flow share-based payment add-back R$178M (ITUB_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp). Bank: last_fcf is FCFE = TTM NI to owners of the parent (FY25 44,857 - 1H25 21,644 + 1H26 23,615 = 46,828) less ~R$17.7bn CET1 retention to fund ~10% loan/RWA growth; reported_fcf = NI + SBC (street basis). Interest income is the bank's revenue, not an excess-cash return, so interest_income = 0.
inputs.fcf_definition: Bank FCFE, not owner FCF: NI to owners of the parent (after NCI, after SBC) minus the CET1 capital retained to keep CET1 at today's 12.3% of RWA as the balance sheet grows. Equivalent to residual income on tangible book: value = tangible equity + PV of (ROTE - CoE) x tangible equity.
inputs.payout_note: FY2025 cash dividends/IOC paid R$48.3bn (includes the extraordinary distribution that cut equity 211,090 -> 204,501); FY2025 declared gross dividends+IOC R$33.7bn = 72.0% payout of recurring managerial result (20-F). Bylaw minimum 25%. A 72% payout at ~24% ROTE is consistent with ~7% book growth (1 - g/ROTE), which is what the base retention path implies.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts BRL (model) to USD (quote): 1/5.2223 = 0.191487, Yahoo Finance BRL=X 5.2223 at 2026-10-03T09:58Z (52-week range 4.88-5.62). Flows, book and the cost of equity are all in BRL; conversion happens only at the per-share output, so intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are USD per ADS and comparable to current_price; the *_brl twins are R$ per preferred share, comparable to ITUB4.SA R$44.83. No forward BRL depreciation is applied to the value: it is embedded in the BRL cost of equity (see wacc_rationale).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 15.0% in BRL, one rate across all scenarios (risk charged once, via paths and weights). Built USD-first then translated: 10y UST ~4.2% + Brazil country risk premium ~2.5% (BB-rated sovereign, ~200-250bp CDS) + beta ~1.0 x 5.0% mature ERP = ~11.7% USD; translated to BRL at the long-run inflation differential (~3.2pp: market breakeven ~5.5% vs US ~2.3%) -> 1.117 x 1.032 - 1 = 15.3%, rounded to 15.0% because the Selic is in an easing cycle (15.00% peak -> 13.75% Sep-2026, consensus ~10.5% by 2028). Local cross-check: 10y NTN-F ~13% + ~2pp equity premium over a sovereign that already carries Brazil credit risk = ~15%. Market-implied: at R$44.83, ~25% ROTE and 7% growth the price implies a ~13.7% BRL CoE.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: occupancy and IFRS-16 depreciation/interest are inside G&A, i.e. inside pre-tax income. lease_cost_pct_path = 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the flow: margin path is calibrated to NI attributable to owners of the parent (TTM NCI ~R$1.0bn, mainly Itaú Chile's 32.6% minority, excluded). No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker' -> residual income on tangible book. Run through the component engine as FCFE at cost of equity (house precedent for banks: HDB, HSBC, NAB.AX, USB, WFC), which is the same economics expressed as distributable cash; exit P/TB per scenario is the Gordon-implied value at year 10 and is checked against ITUB's own trading history. Deposits and funding are operating liabilities, net debt = 0; OCF is meaningless (CSV OCF swings 7bn -> 130bn). ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = managerial Operating Revenues (NII + fees + insurance), TTM = 175.1 - 88.1 + 93.4 = R$180.4bn (Q4-2025 and Q2-2026 releases). 'ebitda' is a pre-tax-equivalent to-parent margin: NI to parent / revenue / (1 - 28%) + SBC 0.1%; TTM NI 46,828 / 180,400 = 25.96% of revenue -> 36.15%. Tax 28% is a calibration rate, not the IFRS ETR: IFRS 1H26 ETR was ~10% (2,783 / 26,982) because tax effects of the hedge of overseas investments and IOC deductibility sit in the tax line; only the after-tax NI level matters for value. D&A = 0 (inside G&A). 'capex' = CET1 retention = CET1(t-1) x RWA growth(t) / revenue(t), starting CET1 R$194.7bn (12.3% of RWA 1,582bn, Q2-2026 Note on capital); RWA grows ~2pp faster than revenue in years 1-2 (loans +10% YoY while Selic cuts compress spreads). CET1 12.3% is held, not run down, so no excess capital is credited in the bridge (CET1 fell 13.1% -> 12.3% YoY). TANGIBLE BOOK: equity to parent 217,779 - goodwill & intangibles 26,313 = R$191.5bn = R$17.18 per diluted share (US$3.29); current price = 2.61x TBV, 2.29x BV (R$19.54 per diluted share; company-reported BVPS in circulation R$19.76). HISTORICAL P/B (year-end ITUB4 price on today's share basis / IFRS BVPS on the same basis): 2015 1.41x, 2016 1.81, 2017 2.07, 2018 2.54, 2019 2.65, 2020 2.17, 2021 1.35, 2022 1.47, 2023 1.76, 2024 1.44, 2025 2.15; median 1.81x book (~2.05x tangible at today's ~12% goodwill share), range 1.35-2.65x book (~1.5-3.0x tangible). IFRS ROE on average equity 2015-2025: 13.5% (2020 COVID) to 22.9%; 18-22% typical; TTM ROTE ~25%. Year-10 exit P/TB implied by Gordon: bear 1.55x, base 1.96x, bull 2.47x - inside the historical band; caps (11/12/13x FCFE) sit just above Gordon so Gordon binds in all three.
inputs.data_caveats: Pre-2018 and pre-2025 per-share history is on a different share basis (bonus issues 2018 +50%, Mar-2025 +10%, Dec-2025 +3%); all per-share history here is restated to today's basis, and growth is measured on NI and total equity. FY2025 equity fell despite record NI because of the R$48.3bn cash distribution - a payout, not value destruction. Colombia/Panama retail sale (closed 31-Jul-2026, ~R$2.5bn) is not separately credited: it is small (~1% of equity) and frees capital already inside the CET1 path.

bear.margin_rationale: Post-election fiscal slippage forces Selic back up in 2027, BRL sells off, and an over-indebted consumer drives cost of credit from ~2.7% toward ~4% of loans: NI/revenue 25% in year 1, 20.5% in year 2 (ROE ~19%, a milder repeat of the 2020 13.5% trough on a much stronger franchise), recovering only to ~21.5% as digital banks permanently take fee and card share. ROTE ~20.5% at year 10 - still above CoE, as Itaú has been in every year since 2015.
bear.exit_rationale: Gordon binds (10.5x); implied year-10 exit 1.55x tangible book (~1.35-1.45x book), the 2021/2024 trough multiples.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) +7%: 2026 guidance NII with clients +5-9% with H2 acceleration, loans +5.5-9.5% (running ~10%), fees cut to +2-5%. Then ~8% as Selic cuts revive credit demand, fading to 6% nominal BRL (~3.5% inflation + ~2.5% real) by year 9.
base.margin_rationale: NI to parent / revenue 26.0% (TTM 25.96%, year-1 NI ~R$50bn, +7%) fading 0.15pp/yr to 24.5% as Nubank/Inter/C6 compete away fee and card economics. ROTE ~25% now, ~23.7% at year 10; payout ~70-74%, matching the 72% FY2025 payout.
base.capex_rationale: CET1 retention: CET1(t-1) x RWA growth [9, 8.5, 8, 7.5, 7, 7, 6.5, 6.5, 6, 6]% / revenue(t); CET1 held at 12.3%.
base.exit_rationale: Gordon binds (11.8x terminal FCFE); implied year-10 exit 1.96x tangible book, ~the historical median (~2.05x tangible / 1.81x book).

bull.margin_rationale: Selic falls to ~10% by 2028 with a credible fiscal anchor after the Oct-2026 election: funding costs drop faster than asset yields, cost of credit eases from ~2.7% toward ~2.2%, efficiency moves from 37.4% toward 35%. NI/revenue rises 26.5% -> 28%; ROTE ~27-28%. Loan growth 10% for three years on credit-penetration runway.
bull.capex_rationale: CET1 retention at RWA growth = revenue growth (min 10% cap in years 1-3).
bull.exit_rationale: Gordon binds (12.5x); implied year-10 exit 2.47x tangible book, inside the 2018-19 peak band (2.5-2.65x book).

entry_price.hurdle_note: Flows are BRL, so the hurdle is set in BRL: the house 15% USD hurdle plus ~3.5pp expected long-run BRL depreciation (inflation differential) = 18.5% BRL. Using 15% BRL would equal the cost of equity and make entry price = intrinsic value.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the house 15% to 25%: the valuation date falls inside the October 2026 presidential election, Brazil's fiscal path is the main swing factor for Selic, BRL and credit costs, and the franchise is ~90% Brazil after the Argentina/Colombia/Panama retail exits. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs a fiscal anchor, a deep Selic easing cycle and margin expansion against intensifying digital competition at the same time. Base 50%: guidance largely intact, ROE ~24%, credit quality stable.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: cyclicality, regulatory single point of failure

sanity_check_note: scripts/sanity_check.py tripped on P/E and P/B because of the known fx_rate direction conflict (memory: sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict): it multiplies the USD ADR price history by inputs.fx_rate (BRL->USD, 0.191487) instead of converting it to BRL, so every historical multiple is understated by ~5.22x (historical P/B 0.04-0.09x, P/E 0.22-0.45x), and its implied-multiples calc divides the BRL weighted IV by the same BRL book/EPS without ever converting the USD price into BRL terms at all, giving implied P/E 1.77x and P/B 0.39x -- both artifacts of mixed currencies, not real multiples. Recomputed by hand in BRL: converting each FY-end USD ADR close to BRL at the current spot rate (1/0.191487 = 5.2223) and dividing by that year's own BRL BVPS/EPS gives a 10yr P/B range of 1.11x-2.48x (avg 1.68x) and P/E range of 5.98x-13.57x (avg 9.24x) -- both plausible bands for a large Brazilian bank. The weighted intrinsic value R.05/share (0.25x27.75 + 0.50x36.90 + 0.25x46.63) implies P/B = 37.05/18.28 = 2.03x (within the 10yr range, not even above the max) and P/E = 37.05/4.01 = 9.24x (exactly at the 10yr average). Conclusion: the trip is a checker comparison-basis defect (fx_rate applied in one direction by dcf_engine.py and the opposite by sanity_check.py, per the memory note), not a driver error, so drivers were NOT changed. Needs the maintainer fix to pick one fx_rate direction across both scripts.
